title: Nour and the River That Argued
logline: Nour fights Dunya until they discover they were always the same water.
story: Certain they were opposites and enemies, Nour, who carried light, ran headlong against Dunya, who was the world and its pull. Each tried to push the other back uphill, and they struggled until both were spent and still. In that stillness Nour noticed they had pooled together and could no longer tell which water had been which. What Nour had fought so hard in Dunya was only the part of Nour that had never been lived. Joined, they became a river wide enough to carry them both.
moral: What you fight hardest in another is most often the unlived part of yourself.
